Let $n>k\geq 1$, let $\Box^n=[-1,1]^n$, and let $H$ be a $k$-dimensional linear subspace. Write $C_{\Box}(n,k)2^k$ for the maximum volume among sections $\Box^n\cap H$ that are affine cubes. **Cube-section affine-cube extremality conjecture.** The maximal volume of a section of the cube $\Box^n$ by a $k$-dimensional linear subspace $H$ is attained on subspaces for which the section is an affine cube; equivalently,

$$
\operatorname{vol}_{k}(\Box^n\cap H)\leq C_{\Box}(n,k)\operatorname{vol}_{k}\Box^k.
$$

This conjecture gives the proposed sharp upper bound in the cases where Ball's general upper bounds are not known to be tight, namely when $k$ does not divide $n$ and $2k<n$.

346197.title: Sturmfels–Uhler polynomiality conjecture for the maximum likelihood degree
346197.assessment: ML degree polynomiality is an intersection-theoretic assertion with a later-resolution lead not checked here; no polynomial fit used as proof.
346197.literal_statement: Let $V$ be a vector space, let $\boldsymbol{S}^2V$ denote the space of symmetric matrices on $V$, and let $c6(n,a)$ be the maximum likelihood degree associated with symmetric matrices of size $n$ and a general $a$-dimensional linear subspace. Sturmfels and Uhler suggest that, for fixed $a$, this invariant is polynomial in $n$. **Sturmfels\Uhler's polynomiality conjecture.** For fixed $a$ the function $c6(n,a)$ is a polynomial in $n$ of degree $a-1$. The theorem preceding the conjecture establishes the formula in several low-dimensional cases and gives all values for $n\leq 6$; the conjecture is presented as an extrapolation from these known values and remains unresolved in the supplied text.

346225.title: Bethe quantum-number conjecture for the maximal six-vertex-model eigenvalue
346225.assessment: Finite-size Bethe root branch and dominant eigenvalue ordering require primary analytic definitions; no formal spectral bridge.
346225.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be the fixed number of Bethe roots, let $H$ be the parameter in the transfer matrix, and let $I_j$ denote the corresponding Bethe quantum numbers. **Bethe quantum-number conjecture.** When the inhomogeneities and $H$ are sufficiently small, or when the system is homogeneous, the maximal eigenvalue corresponds to solutions of the Bethe equations with

$$
I_j=\frac{n+1-2j}{2},\qquad j=1,\ldots,n.
$$

This conjecture identifies the Bethe state describing the largest eigenvalue in the fixed-$n$ subspace. It has a long history in the Bethe-ansatz analysis of the Heisenberg XXZ chain and the six-vertex model, and is used to characterize the ground state and compute the thermodynamic free energy; the stated finite-$N$ claim remains presented as a conjecture here.

346287.title: Mori–Reid–Tian conjecture on disjoint positive-genus curves on complex surfaces
346287.assessment: Complex-surface disjoint curves require full homology-spanning geometry; no configuration or obstruction proved.

346291.title: The maximum-scattered-subspace count conjecture for the family $U_b$
346291.assessment: Finite-field count needs maximum-scattered condition and equivalence classification, beyond counting norm values in a small field.
346291.literal_statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power and let

$$
\Gamma:=\{\operatorname{N}_{q^6/q^3}(b): U_b \text{ is maximum scattered}\},
$$

where

$$
U_b=\{(x,bx^q+x^{q^4}):x\in\mathbb{F}_{q^6}\}.
$$

**The maximum-scattered-subspace count conjecture.**

$$
|\Gamma|=\left\lfloor\frac{(q^2+q+1)(q-2)}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

The quantity $|\Gamma|$ counts pairwise non-$\operatorname{GL}(2,q^6)$-equivalent maximum scattered subspaces of the form $U_b$. The authors state this after proving that $\Gamma$ is nonempty; the conjecture concerns how large the resulting family of inequivalent subspaces is.

346308.assessment: Literal calls chi_e edge-chromatic number, title/source uses perfect-matching index. No routine misdefinition counterexample pursued.

scc(G)=\frac{4}{3}\lvert E(G)\rvert\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \chi'_{e}(G)\leq 4.

346330.title: Bounded critical number conjecture for $I_s$-free triangle-free matroids
346330.assessment: I_s is source-dependent and literal description as projective geometry may be wrong; no altered matroid interpretation used.
346330.literal_statement:
Let $s\geq 4$. An $I_s$-free matroid is a binary matroid with no restriction isomorphic to the $s$-dimensional projective geometry $I_s$, and a triangle-free matroid has no three-element circuit. The critical number of a matroid $M=(E,G)$ is

$$
\chi(M)=\dim(G)-\omega(M^c),
$$

where $M^c$ is the complementary matroid and $\omega(M)$ is the dimension of a largest subgeometry of $M$ contained in $E$.

**Bounded critical number conjecture.** For any $s\geq 4$, the class of $I_s$-free and triangle-free matroids has bounded critical number.

The conjecture asks for a bound on the critical numbers depending only on $s$, not on the dimension of the matroids. The source notes that the result proved there settles the case $s=4$; the cases $s>4$ remain open in the supplied context.

346368.title: The Graovac-Ghorbani index upper-bound conjecture for bicyclic graphs
346368.assessment: See sustained investigation in ATTEMPTS.md; no full-scope endpoint.
346368.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}'_n$ be the family of all bicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices, and let $G\in\mathcal{B}'_n$ have order $n\geq 8$. The Graovac-Ghorbani atom-bond connectivity index is denoted by $ABC_{GG}(G)$. Let $H$ be the graph obtained by adding $n-4$ pendant vertices to one degree-$3$ vertex of $K_4$ with one edge removed. **Upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
ABC_{GG}(G)\leq (n-4)\sqrt{\frac{n-2}{n-1}}+\sqrt{\frac{n-4}{n-3}}+2\sqrt{\frac{n-3}{n-2}}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Equality holds if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $H$. Computational experiments suggest that this graph gives the maximum of the index among all bicyclic graphs for $n\geq 8$.

346372.title: Packing-minima transference conjecture
346372.assessment: See sustained investigation in ATTEMPTS.md; no full-scope endpoint.
346372.literal_statement:
Let $K$ be a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$, let $K_c=\frac12(K-K)$ be its central symmetral, and let $\Lambda$ be a lattice in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Write $[K_c]^\star$ and $[\Lambda]^\star$ for the polar body and dual lattice, respectively, and let $\rho_i(K,\Lambda)$ denote the $i$th packing minimum.

**Packing-minima transference conjecture.** For $1\leq j\leq n$,

$$
\rho_j(K,\Lambda)\,\rho_{n-j+1}([K_c]^\star,[\Lambda]^\star)\geq\frac12.
$$

This is proposed as a complete packing-minima analogue of the lower bound in Banaszczyk's transference inequality. The statement is open in the source.

346388.title: Quillen's conjecture on the poset of elementary abelian p-subgroups
346388.assessment: Full Quillen implication spans all finite groups, primes and order-complex contractibility; no low-order search can prove it.
346388.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $p$ be a prime dividing $|G|$. Let ${\mathcal{A}}_p(G)$ be the poset of non-trivial elementary abelian $p$-subgroups of $G$, ordered by inclusion, and let $|{\mathcal{A}}_p(G)|$ denote its geometric realization. Let $O_p(G)$ be the largest normal $p$-subgroup of $G$. **Quillen's conjecture.** If $|{\mathcal{A}}_p(G)|$ is contractible, then $O_p(G)\neq 1$. This is Quillen's conjecture relating the topology of the poset of elementary abelian $p$-subgroups to the existence of a nontrivial normal $p$-subgroup. The paper proves a strong version of the conjecture for most finite classical groups in non-defining characteristic, but the stated implication is not resolved in full generality here.

346457.title: Odd-uniformity Erdős–Gallai threshold conjecture for link graphs
346457.assessment: Asymptotic link-graph density conjecture requires source eg definition; inherited search-only alias matches are not a prior proof or review.
346457.literal_statement:
Let $1\leqslant d\leqslant k-2$, and set $\ell=k-d$. Let $\mathrm{eg}(\ell)$ be the smallest edge-density threshold such that every sufficiently large $\ell$-uniform hypergraph above that density contains a tightly connected subgraph with a fractional matching of density greater than $1/(\ell+1)$ and edge density greater than $1/2$.

**Odd-uniformity link-graph conjecture.** When $k-d$ is odd, $\mathrm{eg}(k-d)$ is attained by the $(k-d)$-uniform link graphs of the Han–Zhao construction.

The link graphs give the lower bounds $\mathrm{eg}(1)\geqslant1/2$ and $\mathrm{eg}(3)\geqslant5/8$. The source says the coincidence is believed but provides no proof of the asserted attainment.

346499.title: The asymptotic gonality-point equality conjecture for binary curves
346499.assessment: For every fixed gonality, equality must hold for all sufficiently large genus; one explicit cover or genus sequence is not full scope.
346499.literal_statement:
Let $N_2(g,\gamma)$ denote the maximum number of $\b5\mathbb{F}_2$-rational points on a curve of genus $g$ and gonality $\gamma$. For a curve over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with a degree-$\gamma$ morphism to $\mathbb{P}^1$, one has $\#C(\mathbb{F}_2)\leq 3\gamma$.

**Gonality-point equality conjecture.** Fix $\gamma\geq 2$. For $g$ sufficiently large,

$$
N_2(g,\gamma)=3\gamma.
$$

The conjecture asserts that, after the low-genus obstructions disappear, the elementary gonality-point upper bound is attained. The supplied text does not indicate whether this has been resolved.

346602.title: The character sum cancellation conjecture for rough integers
346602.assessment: Uniform oscillatory rough-integer character sum needs all q,x,y,alpha and source constant conventions; no finite experiment proves uniform cancellation.
346602.literal_statement:
Let $q$ be large and let $\chi$ be a non-principal character modulo $q$. For real numbers $x$ and $y$ satisfying

$$
\log q\leq y\leq x,
$$

and writing $P(n)$ for the largest prime factor of $n$ and $e(\alpha)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}$, **the rough character sum conjecture.**

$$
\max_{\alpha\in[0,1]}\left|\sum_{\substack{n\leq x\\P(n)>y}}\frac{\chi(n)}{n}e(\alpha n)\right|\ll 1.
$$

If true, this would make the inequalities in the paper's main lower bounds equalities, supporting the claim that those results are best possible; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
